prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Miami after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Miami for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
Here are six Miami-area personal injury firms you should call after a car accident, with why each is worth contacting. If you want, I can look up their phone numbers and websites for you.

1) Podhurst Orseck PA (Miami)
- Why call: Long-established Miami litigation firm that handles catastrophic injury and wrongful-death cases and has trial experience in high-value matters. Good if your injuries are serious or there may be complex liability issues.

2) Colson Hicks Eidson (Miami/Coral Gables)
- Why call: Miami-headquartered firm with strengths in catastrophic injury, product liability and maritime cases. Strong trial record and experience handling complex medical- and evidence-heavy claims.

3) Morgan & Morgan (Miami)
- Why call: Large national plaintiff firm with a Miami office and substantial resources (investigators, medical experts). Frequently handles motor-vehicle crashes, uninsured/underinsured motorist claims and can move quickly on investigations. Works on contingency (no recovery, no fee).

4) Kanner & Pintaluga (Miami)
- Why call: Miami-based trial firm known for catastrophic injury and high-value recoveries. Good choice when serious injuries and long-term care issues are involved and you need aggressive representation.

5) Steinger, Greene & Feiner (Florida offices including Miami-area)
- Why call: Florida personal-injury firm that focuses on car accidents and has experience with insurance negotiations and litigating when insurers refuse fair settlements. Often handles common crash cases efficiently.

6) Anidjar & Levine (Miami area presence)
- Why call: Personal-injury practice that handles motor-vehicle crashes, wrongful death and uninsured motorist claims. Often offers free consultations and contingency-fee arrangements; good for routine to moderately complex crashes.

How to pick which to call first
- Severity and complexity: prioritize firms with trial and catastrophic-injury experience if your injuries are severe or liability is contested. For more routine claims, the mid-size firms can be more responsive and cost-effective.
- Resources: large firms can deploy investigators and medical experts faster; smaller boutique firms may give more direct lawyer attention.
- Fee arrangement: confirm contingency fee percentage, who pays costs, and how medical liens will be handled.
- Trial willingness: ask if they’ll take your case to trial if necessary (not all firms just settle).

What to ask on the initial call
- Do you handle car-accident cases like mine? Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- Do you take cases on contingency? What percentage and what costs am I responsible for?
- What is your experience with cases involving my injury type?
- What results have you achieved in similar cases (verdicts/settlements)?
- How will you investigate my case and what is the expected timeline?
- Will you handle uninsured/underinsured motorist claims if needed?

Immediate practical tips
- Seek medical care and follow instructions from providers.
- Preserve evidence: photos of scene/vehicles/injuries, contact info for witnesses, police report number.
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other driver’s insurer without talking to a lawyer.
- Notify your insurer as required but keep statements brief; consult a lawyer before signing releases.

If you want, tell me:
- Date and location of the crash, severity of injuries, and whether the other driver is insured — I can prioritize which of these firms likely best fits your situation and fetch phone numbers/links.
